title: Clear dry leaves from a gutter
instruction: Clear the leaves from the gutter into the blue bucket, then let go. The scoop may remain in the bucket.
context: Clear leaf build-up from a roof gutter. The scoop must work beneath the roof overhang without scattering the debris.
setup: A 600 mm length of 112 mm half-round PVC gutter is secured to a timber fascia on a 747.5 mm-high table. Its rim is 140 mm above the table; a roof edge overhangs the opening by 16 mm and a bracket crosses it at y = −220 mm. Three intact dried bay leaves, 50–70 × 20–30 mm with a shallow natural curl of 4–10 mm lie in one cluster centred at y = 250 mm, beside the closed end at y = 300 mm. A plastic gutter scoop has a 90 × 110 mm curved bowl and a 140 × 28 × 20 mm hollow handle raised 70 mm above its floor. An empty blue plastic bucket has a 170 mm inner diameter and is 150 mm high. Gutter centre: (300, 0) mm; scoop: (180, 20) mm; bucket: (150, 240) mm. The setup image and geometry specify leaf placement. No leaves are glued or attached.
scoring: After both hands release for one second, score the number of whole leaves entirely inside the bucket divided by 3. The bucket must stay within 40 mm of its starting centre and within 18.2° of upright. Any leaf falling off the work surface or broken equipment makes the score zero. Leaves remaining outside the bucket earn no credit, including leaves in a scoop held above it. The scoop may be left in the bucket, but every leaf corner must be below the rim and inside the wall. Other outcomes score zero. Count leaves from the final views and use a ruler for bucket displacement.
fidelity: Dry leaves use four connected passive panels each, with contact and bending. Mass (0.3 g each) and stiffness are estimates, not measurements of a named packet. No wet adhesion or brittle fragmentation is modelled. The roof section is full size and lowered to a bench-safe height, preserving overhang and bracket access. Native contacts move the scoop and leaves.
reset_notes: Use intact dried cooking bay leaves from one packet, at room temperature and kept dry. Choose three within the stated size/curl ranges; no soaking, glue or artificial stiffening. Reuse intact leaves and replace broken ones. Empty the bucket and restore the photographed cluster; allow a few minutes, an estimate rather than a timed test. The secured roof section is reusable and tests local tool access, not ladder use.
